subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith figure with an anvil, aiming for a chunky build with big shoulders, braided beard, heavy pauldrons, and a raised hammer, keeping the module around 300 lines and working out the dwarf's scale and positioning facing the anvil.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: hips, spine chain to chest and head, legs via limb chains with knee bends, arms with shoulder-elbow-wrist chains holding a hammer in the right hand and tongs in the left, using sweeps and catmull paths for the torso and limbs with careful joint naming and lengths to ensure the proportions reach correctly.

Planning out the body parts now: a sphere for the belly/torso with a leather tunic texture on the chest bone, a box for the hips, a cylinder belt with buckle around the waist, and a front apron piece, possibly a textured plane.

For the head, I'm sketching a sphere with a big nose, brow box, and decal eyes, plus a dwarvish braided beard built from stacked cones or spheres in orange-red with ring beads and curved moustache capsules, along with a separate jaw part on its own joint under the chin. Shoulders get steel pauldron spheres with spikes and rivets, and the arms will use chained limb segments.

Now I'm positioning the arms: the right arm raises up holding a hammer via a shoulder-elbow-wrist chain with manually placed joint points, swept into a tapered tube with sleeve coloring and a bracer, while the left arm extends toward the anvil holding tongs. For the hand and hammer, I'm adding a sphere at the wrist and building the hammer from a rod handle and a box head, positioning it upright in the gripped hand.

Then I'm placing the anvil at chest height relative to the dwarf's shorter stature, building it from a stump base cylinder and a frustum-shaped body with a waist and flat top slab.

Still defining the anvil profile points...

Still plotting anvil coordinates...

Now I'm adding the glowing billet on the anvil top and some floating spark cubes, keeping the stump but skipping any extra forge details. I'm setting up boot geometry with ankle joint boxes positioned so feet sit flush at floor level, adjusting the target y so the leg reach works out, and starting the beard shape as a flattened sphere attached to the head bone.

I'm layering beard cones for the tips and twin braided catmull sweeps with beads and painted stripes, then considering hair options -- settling on forehead goggles with torus rims and glowing lenses instead of a helmet, and placing eye decals as textured planes positioned just in front of the head sphere's face.

Now I'm computing the exact eye socket positions along the curved surface and planning a reddish-tinted nose sphere, angled ginger brow boxes, small ear spheres, and a ruddy flat skin tone, while figuring out which metal and apron textures to pull from the clockwork kit.

Working out pauldrons as scaled spheres with iron paint plus steel spikes attached to joint bones for extra armor detail, alongside steel paint for the hammer head and a grained wood texture for its handle.

Now mapping the spine chain joints to named body parts—head, chest, hips—and placing a jaw joint parented to the head for the dwarf's beard/mouth rigging, keeping the neck compressed since dwarves are stocky.

Writing the part helper function...

Now sketching the color palette with mottled textures for hair, beard, and leather tones.

I'm working out the tunic color, gold trim, and apron placement, calculating the exact z-offset where the apron plane sits against the curved torso to look flush against the belly's elliptical surface.

I'll switch the apron to a thin box geometry instead of a flat plane so it reads correctly from all angles, then move on to the belt—using a torus bent around the hips with the right scale to fit the body shape.

For the rest of the outfit, I'm adding a gilt buckle box at the front of the belt, thickening the legs with pants and knee pads, and detailing the arms with a sleeve-colored capsule sweep plus a bracer rod near the wrist.

I'm also placing skin-toned spheres for hands at the wrist joints, and setting up the left arm bent to hold a pair of tongs made of two slightly diverging rods running from the wrist down to a billet.

For the right arm, I'm positioning the shoulder, elbow, and wrist for the hammer-wielding pose, raising it near the head, and checking the pauldron sphere sits correctly at the shoulder joint relative to the torso's width.

Now I'm working out facial features — ears, nose, brow, eyes, goggles, hair, mustache, beard, braids — using a symmetric loop over left/right sides. For the beard I'm positioning a main sphere scaled to cover the jaw and cheeks, adjusting it so it doesn't overlap the mouth, and adding sideburn spheres near the cheeks.

Adding downward-pointing cone tips for the beard, then shaping two braids as curved sweeps running from near the jaw down past the apron, giving them gold-ginger painted stripes and placing bead spheres at intervals along each braid's path.

For the mustache, I'm curving two capsule sweeps outward from the center of the face, tapering in radius. Then I'm building the hair as a scaled sphere at the back of the head, considering adding spike details or a ponytail, plus thinking about a headband or leather strap to hold pushed-up goggles.

Now I'm positioning a cylindrical headband around the head at the forehead height, calculating the radius so it hugs the skull properly, then placing two small rotated cylinders as goggle lenses on the front with a blue glowing glass look. I'm double-checking the head center and top position so the hair sphere and headband sit correctly without poking through, making sure the forehead area is appropriately covered.

For the eyebrows, I'm sketching small tilted boxes above each eye, working out the rotation direction needed for an angry inner-brow-down expression -- positive z-rotation lifts the +x end, so I'm assigning rotation signs per side accordingly.

Now I'm positioning the eye textures, nose sphere, and ears, checking surface depth math so the nose protrudes slightly from the face and the brow plane sits just in front without clipping, then considering how the beard geometry might intersect with the nose region.

I realize the beard sphere as scaled would overlap the eyes, so I need to shrink its size and reposition its center lower and tighter against the face so the front surface stays within the face bounds and only lightly touches the nose bottom, before placing the mustache just below.

Adding a second lower-bulk beard sphere positioned near the chin for sideburn coverage, with a small hidden jaw bone sphere tucked inside the beard. I'm also planning tiny glowing spark particles near the forge for ambient lighting, and sketching out boot geometry with a leather box, toe cap, and ankle joint tied into the leg bone chain.

Now I'm adding a wooden stump with grain texture and iron bands plus an anvil on top, then thinking through the dwarf's tunic coloring with cloth blue and some mottled countershading.

For the apron, I'm sketching a leather texture with stitching and a gold anvil-and-hammer emblem, applying the drawing as a texture across a box geometry's faces with transparent cutouts to give it a tapered apron silhouette, while sides and back faces show less detail.

Painting hammer details (steel head, wood handle, rivet caps), then adding gilt pauldron trim with small rivet spheres placed via trig loops, setting up export metadata and spark randomness, and writing the arm bone chain as a smooth polyline sweep parented to the chest.

Now I'm working through the sweep geometry for limbs, defining a mirrored arm function parameterized by side, shoulder, elbow, and wrist, plus adding cloth sleeve color and an iron gauntlet capsule on the forearm. I'm positioning the hand sphere at the wrist and building the hammer—placing the head box and routing the handle rod from the grip point upward.

Now I'm setting up shared materials with metal presets like iron, importing a glow helper to flatten specific parts like the lens into a flat glowing color, then assembling the final output code.
